findings.title: T-4's Test does not prove AC-10's stated observable
quotes: Independent test:** run `uv run python tests/test_pack.py -v`.
findings.fix: add to T-4's Test field "and `uv run python tests/test_pack.py -v` exits 0 with more than 0 tests run", so the task's done-check matches AC-10's observable.

sources.situation: T-4's Test field names only TC-10, which runs a synthetic `script(tmp, ...)` with two passing tests. The spec's independent test runs `tests/test_pack.py -v`. A worker can pass TC-10 and still find `uv run python tests/test_pack.py -v` printing `no test named -v` if that script reaches `main` through a path the synthetic one does not. Nothing in T-4 asks the worker to run the real script.

findings.note: T-4's Test line also runs tests/test_pack.py -v and expects exit 0 with tests run

findings.title: T-1 bundles two order-sensitive contracts at strong/med
quotes: Tier: strong: ledger state with clear integration tests, but the forgery cases need care
raised before the ledger is saved, so no round, finding or outcome is recorded
before anything is merged or saved
findings.fix: either raise T-1 to max with effort high, or split it into a refuter-batch task (CT-1, CT-2; TC-1, TC-2, TC-3, TC-13, TC-15, TC-16) and a judged-version task (CT-3; TC-11, TC-12) with the next free ID, and make T-3 depend on the refuter-batch task.

sources.situation: T-1 changes `collect`, `ask_refuter`, `refuter_pack`, `step` and `refute` in jury.py for CT-1 and CT-2, adds the judged-version refusal in `collect` for CT-3, and lands eight tests across two test files. Both CT-1 and CT-3 require their refusal to fire before a save or merge, in the same few functions. A worker who saves `asked[run]` or the merged outputs ahead of the version check can leave a refused call with a recorded change. A strong/med worker holding this in one context is the case the tier note itself flags as needing care.

findings.reason: tasks-executability: only T-1's effort moved (med to high). Tier stays strong, and T-1 is not split, so neither option the finding asked for is done.
findings.note: Delegated (human's standing authority, lazy and minimal): T-1 stays one strong task at high effort; the order the finding fears (a save before the refusal) is caught by TC-1 and TC-11, which assert the ledger's round is unchanged after a refusal, and the implementation jury reviews it

findings.title: CT-5 and TC-6 name different git diff commands
quotes: the patch file is `git diff --binary`'s stdout through CT-4 with `raw=True`
the saved patch's bytes equal `git diff --cached --binary --no-renames <base>` run in the worktree
findings.fix: name one exact diff command in CT-5 and use the same command verbatim in TC-6's Assert.

sources.situation: CT-5 says the saved patch is `git diff --binary`'s stdout. TC-6 expects the bytes of `git diff --cached --binary --no-renames <base>`. A worker who follows CT-5 may write a patch with different flags. TC-6's single edit gives the same bytes either way, so the test would still pass. A change that git detects as a rename, though, would then be checked against bytes the worker never produced.

findings.note: Delegated (human's standing authority): CT-5 names the family, land and shelve use different git diff commands by design; TC-6 tests land and names land's exact command, so a worker following CT-5 for land produces those bytes
